Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Global BPO Management team, within Robinhood Customer Care Operations, is responsible for the strategy, governance, performance, and commercial management of Robinhood's global Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) partner network. We support key operational areas including Customer Experience, Financial Crimes, Fraud, Account Operations, and Credit to ensure our partners operate efficiently and compliantly. Our team fosters a collaborative and supportive culture that values analytical rigor, open feedback, and continuous learning. We work closely with our partners to deliver exceptional support experiences to our customers! Together, we focus on building scalable solutions that help democratize finance for everyone.

As the Manager, Global BPO Management, you will lead and develop a team of Vendor Managers and Performance Analysts. You will serve as the strategic owner of Robinhood's outsourced operations, overseeing partner relationships, operational performance, and commercial health. In this role, you will collaborate with teams in Product, Finance, and Compliance to drive long-term network strategy and risk diversification. You will balance strategic leadership with hands-on execution to help optimize processes and reduce operating costs. Your leadership will directly influence partner performance and ensure our customers receive high-quality care!

This role is based in our Chicago, IL, Denver, CO and Westlake, TX offices, with in-person attendance expected 5 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Vendor Managers and Performance Analysts, fostering a culture of accountability, analytical rigor, and continuous professional growth.
  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for our global BPO partner network, overseeing operational performance, service delivery, and compliance across all partners.
  • Establish operational reporting frameworks and analytical models to translate performance metrics into clear, actionable business strategies.
  • Drive continuous process improvement and cost optimization by conducting root cause analysis and implementing scalable operational solutions.
  • Coordinate with internal department leaders in Product, Finance, and Legal to execute vendor agreements, manage budgets, and align vendor operations with company goals.

What you bring

  • Proven track record of managing global vendor networks, including executing operational governance, service level agreements, and financial budgeting.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience using platforms like Looker, Tableau, or SQL to translate operational metrics into clear strategic decisions.
  • Experience negotiating and managing commercial contracts, including Master Service Agreements (MSAs) and Statements of Work (SOWs).
  • FINRA Series 7, 63, and 9/10 or Series 24 licenses (strongly preferred, or willingness to obtain).

Our ambitious roadmap requires a great culture shaped by exceptional leaders. Here’s what we expect from them:

  • Hire and retain top talent by setting a high bar, hiring only those who raise it, investing in onboarding, and addressing talent issues quickly and fairly.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is seeking a Fraud Operations Manager to help build and lead a team of Fraud Operations Specialists responsible for the efficient and effective execution of fraud detection and prevention strategies across all of Ramp’s products, enabling Ramp’s rapid growth. This role requires the ability to balance people management, process engineering, strategic thinking, and planning.   • Partner with risk strategy teams to create a closed loop process to enhance policies and procedures

  • Research emerging fraud trends to innovate on Ramp's decisioning systems and policies

  • Help coordinate and respond to incidents through on-call duties as needed – in addition to customer escalations or sensitive case handling

  • Partner with Customer Support to educate and create awareness on fraud prevention best practices, identifying social engineering attempts, and support customers

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in risk management including account takeovers and a broad range of payment related fraud

  • Minimum 2 years of experience building and managing teams

GoMining is a Bitcoin cloud-mining platform that has grown into a full crypto ecosystem: Digital Miners, the GOMINING token, GoMining Card, Wallet, Simple Earn, the VIP programme and Miner Wars. We’re growing fast and plan to multiply sales next year. A large part of that growth will come from partners who already have big audiences.

This role brings those partners in across Asia. We’re hiring one BDM per region, and this position covers the Asian market. You’ll find and sign affiliates and partners with large networks in Asia: crypto exchanges and media, iGaming operators and affiliate networks, brokers, fintech players, streamers and influencer agencies. Our offer to them is one of the strongest on the market: a high commission on every sale their audience makes, plus a lifetime revenue share. Your job is to put that offer in front of the right people and close the deal.

This is not a desk job and not mass cold outreach. You’ll spend much of your time in the field, at conferences, expos and meetings across Asia, holding live negotiations every day. You’ll be one of the first members of a regional BD team we’re building from scratch. Your income grows directly with the volume your partners bring in, and the bonus is uncapped.

What you’ll do

Hunting: find the partners who matter

  • Map the partners with the biggest reach in Asia: crypto (exchanges, wallets, media, communities), iGaming and gambling (operators, affiliate networks, streamers), brokers (forex, CFD, investment platforms), fintech and payments, large media and influencer agencies.
  • Work the field: attend crypto, iGaming, affiliate and fintech conferences across Asia, book meetings in advance and close partnerships on site.
  • Use your own network and local reputation to get in front of decision-makers, not just whoever answers an email.

Closing: run the full cycle

  • Own every deal end to end: first contact, negotiation, agreeing terms, onboarding, launching traffic and the first sales.
  • Negotiate with founders and senior management, and show clearly what partnering with GoMining is worth to them and their audience.
  • When a partner says no, find out why and bring that back so we can sharpen the offer.

Growing: turn partners into volume

  • Grow the partners you’ve signed: higher volume, new formats, and special offers for their audiences.
  • Keep your pipeline up to date in the CRM, report weekly on the funnel, and file a short results report after every trip.
  • Share what you see in the Asian market (competitor offers, partner expectations, local payment specifics) with the team.

What success looks like

  • First month: you know the product and the partner offer inside out, your Asia pipeline is mapped, and your conference and meeting calendar for the next quarter is set.
  • First 3 months: you’re running a steady rhythm of in-person meetings, your first partnerships are signed and live, and the first sales are coming in through your partners.
  • Ongoing: we measure you on new active partners per month, sales volume and revenue from those partners, and how well your meetings convert into signed deals.
  • 3+ years in business development, partnerships or affiliate management in crypto, iGaming, gambling, brokerage or fintech.
  • Your own network in Asia (affiliates, networks, operators, media). This is the main requirement.
  • A track record of closing large partnership deals, with numbers you can walk us through.
  • Confidence negotiating with founders and senior management.
  • Readiness to travel a lot to conferences and meetings across Asia.
  • A hunter mindset: proactive, fast-paced, driven by results and money.
  • Fluent English.

Would be a plus

  • An Asian language: Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian or another language of the region.
  • A personal reputation in the local crypto, affiliate or iGaming community.
  • A strong grasp of affiliate models (CPA, RevShare, hybrid) and traffic.
  • Experience with large affiliate networks and streamers.
  • Knowledge of payment specifics in Asian markets.
  • Sales-driven pay: a fixed salary plus an uncapped bonus on the sales volume your partners bring in.
  • A travel and conference budget for field work across Asia.
  • Fast decisions and direct access to the head of the direction.
  • Professional growth: support for courses, conferences, and English learning (up to 100% coverage).
  • Work-life fit: remote format with flexible hours across international teams.
  • Paid leave: up to 20 vacation days + 8 company holidays + 5 personal days per year.
  • Team culture: retreats in international locations (for example, company apartments in Cyprus).

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Payward Services is an enterprise infrastructure platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate trading, payments, funding, and digital asset services through a single unified system. It provides coordinated liquidity, custody, compliance, risk management, and settlement capabilities, reducing operational complexity for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers.

As the first dedicated Sales Operations Analyst on the team, you’ll support Business Development across PWS and xStocks so our salespeople can spend their time selling. You’ll run RFP and DDQ responses from start to finish, prepare the team for diligence meetings, qualify and route inbound leads, and keep our CRM, pipeline reporting, and customer insights accurate. You’ll report to PWS sales leadership and work closely with Business Operations, Solutions, Legal, Compliance, and Product.

 

The opportunity

  • Own RFP and DDQ responses for PWS and xStocks from kickoff through submission: triage incoming questions, route technical and compliance items to Solutions and Compliance, and make sure answers are validated before they go out

  • Coordinate contributions from Legal, Compliance, Security, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams, establishing deadlines and driving follow-up to ensure timely, complete responses

  • Oversee document assembly and final formatting to ensure every submission is accurate, polished, and delivered on schedule

  • Lead internal preparation and alignment for major client presentations, particularly RFP due diligence meetings, and track action items through to resolution

  • Qualify inbound leads, including follow-up qualifying questions where needed, and route them promptly to the right salesperson or to self-serve onboarding

  • Maintain Attio CRM data integrity, ensuring accounts, contacts, deal stages, and client outreach activity are accurate and consistent with Salesforce and other teams’ systems

  • Build and maintain pipeline reporting in Attio, including stage definitions, funnel metrics, and forecast inputs, and prepare materials for weekly pipeline reviews

  • Manage the handoff from signed deal to onboarding, confirming contracts, pricing, and billing details are in place so Solutions and Finance can start without chasing information

  • Produce weekly customer insights from call notes and CRM activity, summarizing product requests, competitor feedback, and pricing feedback, and communicate emerging trends to Sales, Product, and leadership

  • Develop and maintain a library of approved RFP and DDQ responses, and use it with AI tools to draft accurate, consistent first-pass answers

  • Identify process gaps and implement better workflows, automating repetitive work where possible

  • Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned

 

What you bring

  • 3+ years of experience in sales operations, sales support, or proposal management, ideally within banking, fintech, financial services, or crypto

  • Experience managing RFPs, DDQs, security or compliance questionnaires, or other complex documents with many contributors

  • Proven ability to drive deadlines and coordinate cross-functional stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Security, Product, and other teams

  • Hands-on experience with a CRM platform (Attio experience is a plus; Salesforce or HubSpot experience is transferable)

  • Comfort building simple reports and dashboards

  • Excellent writing, editing, and document formatting skills

  • Clear, confident communication with senior internal stakeholders and external clients

  • Understanding of institutional and B2B sales cycles in financial services

  • Interest in crypto and digital assets (prior industry experience is not required)

  • Proactive, process-oriented approach, with the ability to identify issues and implement effective solutions

  • Rigorous attention to detail

 

Nice to haves

  • Background in banking, institutional sales, or B2B infrastructure and API products

  • Familiarity with vendor due diligence and security questionnaires

  • Experience using AI tools or workflow automation to speed up repetitive sales or operations work

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe Terminal helps our users extend their online presence to the physical world. The Terminal team’s mission is to make accepting in-person payments as easy as accepting online payments with the Stripe API. With Terminal, businesses can unlock in-person payment use cases that fit their business model, whether that’s creating a superb retail experience, extending their website to a pop-up store, or enabling a mobile point of sale at their next event.

Terminal is one of the fastest-growing products at Stripe, and we are building a uniquely powerful unified commerce platform for global enterprises. The platform offers a single integration for in-person payments, fast and low-cost cross-border money movement, AI-powered optimizations and fraud protection, reporting, and differentiated ways to pay.

What you’ll do

As the product manager responsible for enterprise success within Terminal Payments, you’ll deliver an end-to-end payments and commerce platform for enterprise users. You’ll work directly with users and partners to understand their needs, identify investments that serve multiple businesses, and turn those opportunities into products and integrations.

Responsibilities

  • Set a multi-year strategy for Terminal’s enterprise payments capabilities, build alignment, and translate that strategy into roadmaps and measurable objectives and key results
  • Lead product discovery and roadmapping conversations with enterprise users, balancing their specific requirements with investments that benefit Stripe’s broader platform
  • Build integrations that expand Terminal’s enterprise capabilities, including gift cards, private-label credit cards, tax refunds, and third-party point-of-sale systems
  • Evaluate opportunities to meet enterprise loyalty and customer relationship management needs through Stripe-built offerings, and scale host-to-host capabilities for users that operate their own payment gateways
  • Partner with engineering and product teams, including Core Payments, Optimized Checkout Suite, and Agentic Commerce, to deliver integrated experiences and resolve technical and product trade-offs
  • Work with partnerships, marketing, legal, and industry teams on user and partner needs, go-to-market activities, and representing Terminal at trade shows and partner conferences
  • Collaborate with Product Strategy and Operations to deliver in-person support and installation services for enterprise users

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience or equivalent experience
  • Experience working on business-to-business products, ideally with a track record of building for enterprise scale
  • Technical proficiency and systems-thinking skills, ideally with a degree in engineering or computer science
  • Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, including the ability to make complex concepts accessible

Preferred qualifications

  •  Demonstrated success and strong execution track record in building payment products

Since its inception in 2011, Blockchain has earned the trust of over 90 million wallet holders and more than 40 million verified users, facilitating over $1 trillion in crypto transactions.

We are looking for an experienced Communications Lead to help shape the next chapter of Blockchain.com’s product innovation, regulatory strength, and technology story.

As Product Comms Lead, you will manage communications and content around our product announcement pipeline, innovation narrative, licensing wins, and technology thought leadership across Blockchain.com’s consumer and institutional portfolio. You will be responsible for making Blockchain.com highly visible, relevant, and recognized as a leading force in the industry among press and other key stakeholders who engage with our content.

This person will be responsible for making Blockchain.com highly visible, relevant and known as leading the industry with press and other stakeholders who ingest our content. You will lead the tech-forward earned (PR) and owned media strategy and execution across major launches, evergreen blog and thought leadership content, and select regulatory/policy news cycles.

The ideal candidate is equal parts crypto-native storyteller and comms tactician. You aren't just a media hound; you are a strategic comms pro who knows how to position cutting-edge tech, products and regulatory progress so that they accrue to the overall narrative we’re building for Blockchain.com. You understand what makes press tick and can get them to write, but you’re also able to weave a technology story through other channels, from written blog content to executive social to awards submissions.

The right candidate combines a deep literacy of the crypto industry and its influencers (traditional press and emergent) with a proven ability to turn complex financial concepts, products, AI advances and regulatory milestones into compelling storylines, press coverage and content that drives attention, trust and adoption.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Narrative & Strategy: Build and execute a differentiated product and technology comms strategy and narrative for Blockchain.com, sitting at the intersection of consumer and institutional products, AI, and regulatory/compliance.
  • Product Launch Comms: Own end-to-end comms for a consistently full pipeline of product launches. Work with Marketing and Product on comms plans to ensure Marketing’s product campaigns support and are supported by Comms-led work.
  • Regulatory Comms: Lead announcements of licensing, regulatory, and compliance milestones. Input into how Blockchain.com contributes to the wider regulatory and policy conversation.
  • AI Positioning: Define and champion Blockchain.com’s position on AI and storytell around how AI improves what we build internally and in customer-facing products.
  • Tech Media & Influencer Relations: Own key press and influencer relationships and proactive and reactive opportunities across product and technical topics. Widen the set of emerging influencers we reach with innovation news.
  • Thought Leadership: Build high-impact platforms for product, technical, and AI spokespeople, including proactive media opportunities, speaking engagements, product-focused award submissions, and executive social presence.
  • Content Creation: Write compelling product-focused content, including blog posts, press releases, and executive (and occasionally corporate) social posts.

You’ll be part of a hybrid-friendly environment where your unique talents and insights will play a crucial role in building something extraordinary.

Principal Engineer, Data Quality Platform

You'll own data correctness across Talos. You'll lead the data quality engineering team, run BAU data operations, and own reference and security master data, along with the pipelines and platform that deliver it.

Our goal: the data we return to clients is always correct, and we find defects before a client does.

You'll join a small team with the mandate to work independently from product engineering and challenge it. Engineering teams make assumptions about how their systems behave. Your job is to test those assumptions and prove or disprove them with evidence.

 

Responsibilities

Lead AI-first data quality engineering

  • Validate every client-facing endpoint continuously. The focus is our REST and WebSocket APIs. Cloud delivery (S3, Snowflake, Databricks) is also in scope. Assert correctness against independent sources of truth, across every environment and client entitlement.

  • Cover streaming as well as request/response. For WebSocket, that means:

    • Sequencing and gap detection

    • Snapshot-to-increment consistency

    • Reconnect and replay correctness

    • Staleness of live subscriptions

    • Agreement between the streamed view and the REST view of the same state

  • Use adaptive detection, not static thresholds. Learn baselines per endpoint and per market, and let them adjust as "normal" changes. Hand-set limits get noisy, go stale, and teach people to ignore alerts.

  • Apply LLM and agentic tooling to generate checks from API specs and schemas, keep them current as the product changes, and triage alerts before a human sees them. Know when a deterministic rule, invariant or cross-source reconciliation is the better tool.

  • Test resilience and load. Design load, performance and failure-mode tests.

  • When you find a fault, raise it with the owning team with enough evidence for them to act. Drive it to resolution, then add a check that would have caught it earlier.

  • Measure and publish endpoint and field coverage, time to detect, detected-before-client rate and false-positive rate.

Run data governance

  • Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.

  • Own data governance tooling such as OpenMetadata.

Own reference and security master data

  • Lead the build-out of the next-generation security master platform, then run it day to day: new listings, symbol mapping across venues, and increment and contract specs.

  • Design processes for safe updates to security entries, with validation and rollback.

Expand coverage across the firm

  • Over time, extend data quality coverage beyond client APIs to:

    • Trade signals

    • Pre-trade analytics

    • Client post-trade analysis

    • PMS analytics

Qualifications

  • A track record of leading data QA or data quality teams, preferably on market data or other high-throughput, real-time data.

  • A deep understanding of streaming and API behaviour: throughput, WebSocket semantics, ordering, recovery and failure modes.

  • Experience inventorying and testing a large API and data surface end to end.

  • Hands-on experience with data governance: cataloging, lineage, ownership.

  • Experience with performance and load testing of distributed systems.

  • A strong engineering background. You design platforms, not scripts on a cron job, and you build on shared infrastructure rather than creating one-off tooling.

  • Practical experience applying LLM and agentic tooling to engineering problems.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Fraud Architect team helps Stripe’s largest and most complex users manage fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle. We combine deep fraud expertise, technical investigation, and product knowledge to help users understand emerging threats, optimize Radar, and implement durable prevention strategies tailored to their business and risk tolerance. Our goal is to enable users’ growth by proactively reducing fraud while protecting legitimate customer activity and turning frontline insights into better products and defenses.

What you’ll do

Stripe users face fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle, including payment fraud, free-trial farming, multi-account abuse, and usage-based billing exploitation. They need a partner who understands their business, anticipates emerging threats, and helps them put effective protections in place as their business and the threat landscape evolve.

As a member of our Fraud Architect team, you’ll be the fraud and risk specialist embedded in strategic user relationships for a small portfolio of named users, acting as a technical extension of their teams. You’ll help users get more from Radar, build a proactive prevention strategy, and turn complex fraud problems into practical decisions.

This role combines analytical rigor, deep fraud investigation, and product judgment. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how Radar scores and classifies transactions, how integrations and available signals affect its decisions, and where its capabilities and limitations matter for a user. You’ll explain what the evidence supports, investigate what it does not yet explain, and translate both into action: better rules and thresholds, integration guidance, or model and feature gaps to pursue with our product teams.

Your focus is proactive, user-specific risk ownership and durable prevention. You’ll provide user context, communicate implications and next steps, and turn incident findings into an implemented and verified prevention plan. You’ll help build, expand, and evolve defenses as user needs and fraud patterns change.

Responsibilities

  • Own each user’s prevention strategy. Maintain a current risk baseline, threat model, and agreed prevention plan for every assigned account. Understand payment methods, integrations, billing flows, trial and promotion mechanics, existing controls, and risk preferences; identify the top risks and gaps across the full customer lifecycle.
  • Make Radar’s behavior understandable and actionable. Investigate scoring, classification, rule behavior, and signal coverage using transaction evidence and technical context. Explain observed behavior and uncertainty clearly, distinguish configuration or integration issues from potential model or feature gaps, and recommend the right next step for the user and our product teams.
  • Design and improve user protections. Help users configure and optimize Radar for their business model and risk tolerance. Develop and validate user-facing rules, thresholds, and integration recommendations, test their expected impact, and guide approved implementation. Balance fraud prevention with legitimate payment acceptance and false-positive risk, without taking on internal-rule deployment or model operations.
  • Anticipate established and emerging fraud vectors. Investigate payment, account, and behavioral patterns to understand how abuse works and where it may move next. Advise on payment fraud, trial and promotion abuse, multi-accounting, bot activity, and usage-based billing exploitation. Evaluate defenses across payment methods and flows rather than treating each attack surface in isolation.
  • Deliver consistent proactive coverage. Run a weekly risk-health review for every assigned account, including those without active incidents, and share a concise health update. Establish early-warning thresholds and notification paths; translate changes in fraud, disputes, early fraud warnings, approval rates, and false positives into timely user conversations and prevention actions. Lead deeper periodic reviews with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Own follow-through, not just recommendations. Maintain a user action plan with named owners, due dates, expected impact, and implementation status. Follow recommendations through user acceptance, implementation, and verification of effectiveness. Revisit residual risk and adjust controls as traffic, threats, and user priorities change.
  • Connect incident response to durable prevention. During incidents, provide user context and prioritization, coordinate user-facing updates with the account team, conduct merchant-specific root-cause analysis, synthesize findings with Engineering, and translate them into an implemented prevention plan. Verify that prevention measures are implemented and effective after handoff.
  • Turn user evidence into product improvements. Partner with Radar Product, Engineering, and Fraud Data Science to investigate limitations and define actionable requirements. Maintain a cross-user backlog of signal, model, integration, and payment-method gaps with clear owners and follow-up milestones. Advocate for durable fixes, explain progress to users, and help them adopt and validate delivered improvements.
  • Enable others to act. Build reusable playbooks, investigation tools, and prevention frameworks. Train Customer Success Managers, Technical Account Managers, and Account Executives to recognize common fraud patterns, explain risk tradeoffs, and know when to involve a specialist.
  • Build and evolve the program. Shape account segmentation, coverage expectations, tooling, and hiring as the function grows. Work with leadership and partner teams to protect proactive capacity and establish clear incident handoffs. Measure success through current prevention plans and consistent coverage across the portfolio, recommendations implemented and proven effective, and improvements in user risk outcomes—not the volume of analysis produced.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years in a technical role with substantial direct user engagement, such as solutions architecture, technical account management, fraud consulting, professional services, engineering, or technical product work, at a payments company, fintech, risk management platform, or fraud-prevention provider.
  • Hands-on experience investigating fraud or abuse and translating findings into effective controls or user guidance. You can reason about adversarial behavior, payment flows, and the tradeoffs between fraud prevention and legitimate user activity.
  • Depth in payment fraud, account takeover, subscription or trial abuse, multi-accounting, dispute management, and network monitoring programs such as VAMP, ECM, or EFM.
  • Technical depth to understand API integrations, trace data and signal flows, investigate system behavior, and discuss technical limitations and implementation options with engineers. You can connect those details to a user’s business problem.
  • Practical understanding of machine-learning-based risk decisions and rule systems, including how signal availability, model behavior, rules, and thresholds interact. You can explain findings clearly without overstating what the evidence establishes.
  • Strong investigative and data science fundamentals: SQL proficiency and experience using Python, R, or a similar language to test hypotheses, investigate unfamiliar patterns, and evaluate controls. You can assess data quality, account for delayed fraud outcomes, and interpret precision, recall, false positives, and business impact.
  • Experience managing multiple user relationships or technical engagements while maintaining proactive coverage and driving recommendations through implementation and measured results.
  • Strong communication and product judgment. You can explain fraud exposure to a CFO, discuss rule logic and integration behavior with an engineer, and turn a user problem into a clear, prioritized product requirement.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with Stripe Radar or similar fraud-prevention platforms such as Forter, Sift, Ravelin, or Signifyd.
  • Experience designing, testing, and safely tuning fraud rules or thresholds in production, including shadow evaluation, user approval, and post-launch effectiveness reviews.
  • Experience partnering with product managers, engineers, and data scientists to diagnose model or signal gaps and translate user evidence into shipped improvements.
  • Familiarity with device intelligence, alternative payment methods, abuse prevention beyond payments, or usage-based business models.
  • Experience building and scaling a technical advisory function, reusable prevention practices, or a multi-account service model.
